findings.summary: Late loss of homing keeps a previously prepared uncapped joint jog or bypasses the pre-home gantry refusal
Cancel during queued jog write lets the shielded write finish but skips its post-await booking; disconnect cleanup sends no stop
The jog gate and write admission do not reject active homing, although native motion rejects joint jogs there

reproduce: Create a separate archive of 5f74a771. Run the repository backend before adding own test files. Copy unchanged button-gates.r217.backend-probe.py as lcnc-gateway/test_r217_codex.py (used only as a queue-harness module); copy r219.backend-probe.py as test_r219_codex.py, then run the targeted command. conftest installs fake_linuxcnc. Frontend: own node_modules, build lcnc-webui; copy r219.playwright.config.ts there and r219.ctl.ts to e2e/ctl.ts. Use only an own mock on 127.0.0.1:4188.
limits: No native motion/acceptance claimed by the fake CMD recorder. Current-state changes happen before command writing in a real single-worker ThreadPoolExecutor.
Cancellation case allows discarding an unsent jog or stopping one that was sent. No synthetic delay inside the CMD call.
Native code read locally, hashes equal the R202 manifest. No comparison of downstream Debian patches.
No live ports or machine commands. All test processes and own mock stopped. Review/evidence only in the live tree.
Operator withdrawal of joint names on buttons accepted; no new operator question.
harness_notes: Initial probe used a FREE constant not exported by fake_linuxcnc; corrected to native numeric FREE=1.
Initial four-joint fixture retained only the helper default three homed flags; corrected to four true flags before the queued transition. Early harness failures not counted as product evidence.
Full backend collection preceded adding own probes. Dependencies copied from an own previous archive; neither product worktree used for builds/tests.
